Figure 1:Overview of COBRA-Skills.At each round, skills in𝒫t\mathcal{P}_{t}are prioritized using a neural
reward predictor and LinearUCB bonus based onℋt−1\mathcal{H}_{t-1}(\scriptsize1⃝), and the highest-priority skill is evaluated
by the target agent (\scriptsize2⃝). The resulting reward
and trajectories update the optimization history and scoring model
(\scriptsize3⃝). At scheduled population updates (performed
periodically rather than after every round), new skills are evolved from
accumulated evidence (\scriptsize4⃝), and the updated priority scores from \scriptsize1⃝
identify low-priority skills, which are replaced by the newly evolved
skills to form𝒫t+1\mathcal{P}_{t+1}(\scriptsize5⃝).
Dashed borders and arrows indicate scheduled-only operations.

Figure 6:Cross-model transfer of optimized skills.Rows and columns denote the optimization and evaluation target models, respectively. Each cell reports the test score and the gain over the evaluation model’s no-skill baseline; outlined cells indicate in-model
evaluation. GPT-5.5 is used as the teaching model throughout.
